title: Spring Cleaning in an Infant Star System
caption: The ringed dusty disc around the young star HD 169142, imaged by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA)
celestial: HD 169142 · constellation Sagittarius · about 380 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Vivid rings, separated by deep gaps, circle the young star HD 169142 in this image from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA). The rings are thick bands of dust, and ALMA captured them sharply by detecting weak signals from the disc's millimeter-sized grains.

ALMA is built to study cold gas and dust, and it has revealed many young planetary systems with similar gaps and cavities. Several explanations have been proposed, including turbulence from an effect called magnetorotational instability and dust grains fusing together, but the most plausible is that giant protoplanets carved the gaps.

As a planetary system forms, gas and dust gather into planets, which then sweep their orbits clean and herd the leftover material into sharp bands. The deep gaps here fit the presence of several protoplanets, in agreement with optical and infrared studies of the same star. Watching discs like this lets scientists probe the first steps of planet formation.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (0.01 x 0.01 arcminutes) and distance (380 light years), the frame spans roughly 0 × 0 light-years. Its light set out about 380 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: ALMA imaged the disc in millimeter-wavelength light at 1.3 mm, tracing the glow of dust grains. The color mapping isn't published.
filters: 1.3 mm · Millimeter 230 GHz (Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array Band 6)
understand.eye: This millimeter light is invisible to the eye. The image shows the glow of cold dust that visible-light telescopes cannot pick up in this way.

explore: HD 169142 is a young, isolated star about 380 light-years away in the direction of Sagittarius. ALMA recorded this disc at a wavelength of about 1.3 millimeters, using its Band 6 receivers.
alt: A disc around a young star made of rings of dust separated by deep gaps.
